title: Cotangent bootstrap from the diagonal
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(B,B)=0$ for every $i>0$ and that the standard cotangent complex $L_{B/(B\otimes_A B)}$ is zero in the derived category. Then the standard cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] is zero in $D(B)$.

proof.text: Put $D=B\otimes_A B$, with $\iota_1(b)=b\otimes1$, $\iota_2(b)=1\otimes b$, and multiplication $\mu:D\to B$, $\mu(b_1\otimes b_2)=b_1b_2$. The positive self-Tor vanishing allows [lem-trf-cotangent-diagonal-tor-comparison]: its $\gamma:B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to D[0]$ is an isomorphism for the second-factor $B$-action. For the square $(A\to B)\to(B\xrightarrow{\iota_2}D)$ with vertical maps $A\to B$ and $\iota_1$, the same node gives the canonical isomorphism $\beta:L_{B/A}\otimes_{B,\iota_1}^{\mathbf L}D\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{D/B}$ in $D(D)$, with the right-hand cotangent complex relative to $\iota_2$.

source.place: Tag 08R1 (lemma-bootstrap), first sentence invoking Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex); the Tor-to-derived-comparison argument of returned Step 1.

proof.text: For each $b\in B$, $\mu\iota_2(b)=\mu(1\otimes b)=b$, so $B\xrightarrow{\iota_2}D\xrightarrow\mu B$ is a ring retraction. Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-retract-transitivity-vanishing] with $(R,S,j,r)=(B,D,\iota_2,\mu)$. Its transitivity triangle has first term $L_{D/B}\otimes_{D,\mu}^{\mathbf L}B$, zero middle term $L_{B/B}$, and third term $L_{B/D}$ for the multiplication map $\mu$. The latter is zero by the diagonal hypothesis. Thus the node's vanishing clause gives $L_{D/B}\otimes_{D,\mu}^{\mathbf L}B=0$ in $D(B)$.

proof.text: Also $\mu\iota_1(b)=\mu(b\otimes1)=b$. Let $F=-\otimes_{D,\mu}^{\mathbf L}B:D(D)\to D(B)$. Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-retract-scalar-cancellation] to $(j,r)=(\iota_1,\mu)$ and the original map $A\to B$; it gives $\alpha:F(L_{B/A}\otimes_{B,\iota_1}^{\mathbf L}D)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{B/A}$. Since a functor preserves isomorphisms, $F(\beta)\circ\alpha^{-1}$ is an isomorphism from $L_{B/A}$ to $F(L_{D/B})$. Its target is a zero object by Step 2, hence $L_{B/A}=0$ in $D(B)$.
